requirements.text: The same definition of default is applied across the IRB approach, IFRS 9 Stage 3, non-performing exposure reporting and credit risk management, in all Group entities.
requirements.level_reason: Institution-wide requirement on the consistent application of the default definition; evidenced in the Bank's default definition framework and group implementation, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Default is identified at obligor level for all exposure classes, and all credit obligations of a defaulted obligor are flagged as defaulted.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Joint credit obligations and contagion between connected obligors are treated in accordance with section 8 of EBA/GL/2016/07.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The date of default is the first day on which any default criterion is met and is recorded for every default event.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Days past due are counted from the first day on which both the absolute and the relative materiality components are exceeded, and reset when either is no longer exceeded.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The materiality threshold is EUR 100 and 1% for retail exposures and EUR 500 and 1% for non-retail exposures.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; thresholds consistent with RTS 2018/171 and pilot REQ-D07 (retail EUR 100 / 1%).

requirements.text: The absolute component is compared with the sum of all past due amounts of the obligor, and the relative component is that sum divided by the obligor's total on-balance-sheet exposure.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where the repayment schedule is changed, days past due are counted on the modified schedule, and forbearance changes are assessed for distressed restructuring.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Technical past due is recognised only in the situations defined as technical past due in EBA/GL/2016/07, and each case is documented and corrected within 30 days.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Non-accrued status, specific credit risk adjustments (including Stage 3), sale at a credit-related loss above 5%, distressed restructuring with DFO above 1%, bankruptcy and forced sale of collateral lead to default automatically.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard text; triggers consistent with CRR Art. 178(3) and EBA/GL/2016/07 section 5, and with the UTP triggers of the pilot RDS.

requirements.text: Additional UTP indicators (such as fraud, significant income or cash-flow decline, covenant breach, multiple forbearance) lead to a case-by-case assessment completed within 30 days of detection.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Each UTP trigger and indicator is mapped to source-system fields, and the outcome of each case-by-case assessment is recorded with its rationale.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The diminished financial obligation is calculated as the relative reduction in net present value of expected cash flows caused by the restructuring, discounted at the original effective interest rate.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: An obligor returns to non-default status only after at least three months without any default trigger and an assessment that the improvement in credit quality is factual and permanent.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: After a distressed restructuring, the probation period is at least 12 months, and return requires a material payment, no amount past due and no concerns about full repayment.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The probation start date and status are recorded for every default event.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Re-default rates of obligors returned to non-default status are analysed at least annually by default trigger, and longer probation periods are proposed where cure is not permanent.
requirements.level_reason: Periodic review of the Bank-wide default definition; evidenced in the annual default definition review, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Where an obligor defaults again within 12 months of returning to non-default status, both events are treated as a single default starting on the first date of default for risk parameter estimation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The RDS identifies and links multiple default events, and the number of merged default events is reported in the RDS documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The RDS default flag is constructed in accordance with CR-STD-110, including materiality thresholds, UTP triggers, probation periods and the treatment of multiple defaults.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The default flag construction in the RDS code is reconciled with the production default flag for the periods in which both are available, and differences are explained.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: For periods before 1 January 2016 the approximation of the default flag from arrears and restructuring data is documented and its effect on default rates quantified.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: Periods for which the default flag could not be reconstructed with probation periods are stated in the RDS documentation together with the treatment applied.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: The default flags used for IRB and IFRS 9 purposes are reconciled quarterly between the risk and finance systems.
requirements.level_reason: Institution-wide reconciliation between risk and finance systems; evidenced in quarterly reconciliation reports, not in model documentation.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.

requirements.text: A change to the definition of default is assessed as a change to all IRB rating systems under MRM-STD-050 and Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) No 529/2014.
requirements.level_reason: Institution-wide change governance for the default definition; evidenced in the change assessment for the definition of default, not in the documentation of an individual model.
requirements.verification_note: Internal standard (CR-STD-110 v3.0) text authored for the library.
